propositions: Every attested gate resolution materializes a full fresh copy of the ~620 MiB tickets tree to a content-addressed cache entry with key <store>/tickets-<sha>, despite adjacent commits differing by only one or two files

The tickets cache key (live tracker HEAD) advances every ~26 seconds with zero reuse; the same SHA is almost never requested twice, violating the core assumption in ADR 0005 that immutable SHAs are perfect cache keys

Concurrent agents running gate resolutions multiply the write amplification directly; five concurrent agents cycling gates produce single-digit GiB of fresh writes per round on a key that effectively never hits, contributing to sustained CPU spikes and resource starvation
Byte accounting for shared entries over-credits recovered space by summing st_size/nlink per-inode, causing the free-space watermark loop to stop short believing it recovered bytes still on disk

The delta_tree implementation hardlinks unchanged paths between consecutive entries and rewrites only differing paths, but must force .ticket-write.lock into the rewrite set to prevent flock scoped to the inode from blocking across entries
